extracted.intended_audience: poets and writers submitting work to Poetry (Poetry Foundation) magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and letter-to-the-editor guidelines for Poetry magazine covering eligibility (previous publication), submission methods, required metadata, simultaneous-submission policy, payment rates and rights, and editorial handling of letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: One submission at a time per category
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send only one submission at a time per category, and wait until you hear back from us before uploading a new submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do send multiple submissions, they will be archived unread and will receive no response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time / patience
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the number of submissions we receive each year, we will likely get back to you within eight months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our response time can be up to 8 months. We appreciate your patience—we have a small staff who reads over 150,000 poems per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spam filter — ensure delivery of response
rubrics_metrics.description: To make sure you receive our response, set your spam filter to allow emails from [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Only previously unpublished work accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider only previously unpublished work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that has appeared online for any reason, including social media posts, is considered to have been previously published and should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions allowed with notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is open to simultaneous submissions, but let us know immediately if work is accepted elsewhere by adding a note to your submission specifying the work that is no longer available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: All poets will be compensated for published poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For text poems, we pay $10/line with a minimum honorarium of $300 per poem. For visual poems, audio poems, and video poems, we pay $300 per poem. If a piece is published in multiple formats, such as print and video, we pay for each format. For prose, we pay $150 per published page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: How does Poetry pay its contributors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We pay via ACH, wire transfer, check, or JPay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights acquired by the magazine
rubrics_metrics.description: What rights does Poetry acquire for published work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry acquires first serial rights and non-exclusive reprint rights, meaning that all authors can reprint their work as they’d like after it’s appeared in the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary submission platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Please visit our Submittable page for our full submission guidelines and open calls for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click here to be redirected to our online submission manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative email submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to use Submittable for any reason, you may email your submission to [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please include your name, contact information, and cover letter in the body of an email. Please make the subject line of the email “SUBMISSION, [your last name], [submission category].” For instance, a visual poetry submission from Jane Doe would have the subject line “SUBMISSION, Doe, Visual Poetry.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal submissions (with caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unable to use the internet, you may mail your submission to: SUBMISSIONS - POETRY, 61 W. Superior St, Chicago, IL 60654.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please note that we are not currently working in the office due to COVID-19 precautions, so responses to mailed submissions are delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor — content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is looking for thought-provoking responses to work published in the magazine, as well as letters that raise new questions about the state of contemporary poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To send us your letter, please fill out the form here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor — editorial handling and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If we choose to use your letter, we will notify you by phone. If you have not heard from us within two weeks of sending your letter, you may assume we will not be using it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All letters may be edited for length and clarity, and may appear online, in print, or both.
